description: Gifted to the Commonwealth on 1 July 2019 and owned by the RAAF, but based at Temora and on public display with the museum, maintained under contract by Temora Aviation Museum Engineering. Airworthy, registered VH-MHR and flown as MH-R. Confirmed by the RAAF January 2026 heritage fleet review as continuing in flying operations at Temora.

Registered VH-VAM. Appeared at the Fleet Air Arm 60th anniversary airshow at Nowra in 2008 wearing Navy titles and the serial A79-842. Withdrawn from the RAAF heritage fleet in January 2026 and returned to the museum under existing agreements.

Ex-RAF VZ467, the last Meteor F.8 in RAF service, named Winston. Registered VH-MBX and painted as RAAF A77-851, a serial belonging to a different airframe whose cockpit is in South Australia. Withdrawn from the RAAF heritage fleet in January 2026 and returned to the museum.
Ex-RAF target-tug Canberra registered VH-ZSQ. Withdrawn from the RAAF heritage fleet in January 2026 and returned to the museum.
Ryan STM-S2, constructor number 474, in Netherlands East Indies markings. Withdrawn from the RAAF heritage fleet in January 2026 and returned to the museum.
Ex-USAF A-37B registered VH-DLO. Withdrawn from the RAAF heritage fleet in January 2026 and returned to the museum.
Ex-USAF A-37B registered VH-XVA. Part of the 2019 gift; the A-37 was withdrawn from the RAAF heritage fleet in January 2026 and returned to the museum.
Registered VH-LRE and reported on loan to the museum. Survey lists give the identity as 4606/53125; those two numbers have not been reconciled, so no serial is entered.
Ex-USAF forward air control O-2A registered VH-OII; museum-owned and not part of the 2019 Commonwealth gift.

Restored to airworthiness under a 2005 agreement between the RAAF Museum and Temora; first post-restoration flight 16 July 2009, the first Avon Sabre flight anywhere in over sixteen years. Grounded since 2015 over ejection seat certification. The January 2026 RAAF heritage fleet review withdrew the Sabre and listed it for consideration for static display at an approved heritage institution; ADF-Serials last records it held at Temora.
Restoration to airworthiness stopped when Temora signed the agreement to fly A94-983. Reported to carry a constructor plate reading CAC9. In store at the museum.
Instructional airframe No.15 at RSTT Wagga, then on static display at No.1 Central Ammunition Depot, Kingswood NSW. One of three Sabres acquired by Temora in April 2005 and held in store.
Instructional airframe No.12 at RSTT Wagga Wagga from December 1972; one of three Sabres acquired by Temora in April 2005 and held in store.
Instructional airframe No.13 at RSTT Wagga Wagga; one of three Sabres acquired by Temora in April 2005 and held in store.
At the Camden Museum of Aviation until August 2000, then acquired by Temora Aviation Museum to support the operation of A79-617.
